_about: Input sorting for the slice (docs/slice/slice_tech_plan.md 3, Decision 3). The old game and the sandbox share one InputMap (project.godot), so the slice does not rewrite it: at slice boot InputSorting applies the small changes below, and a test proves that no two actions that are live in the same kind of room share a button by accident. contexts: which actions the player can use at once in a town room, a dungeon or arena room, and a menu. room_kinds: rooms.json kind -> context. allowed_overlaps: pairs that share a button on purpose (never live at the same moment). interact_changes: what Decision 3 does to the interact button, per slice.json interact.mode. Pad button numbers are Godot's (0 A, 1 B, 2 X, 3 Y, 6 Start, 9 left shoulder, 10 right shoulder); axis 5 is the right trigger.

allowed_overlaps.why: Enter confirms inside a menu and Start closes the pause menu; the same press never means both because the pause menu eats it (old game's setup).

attack_button.why: Pad B is the dash. The attack button (pad X) talks and uses things; E stays on the keyboard.

own_button.why: Pad B is the dash. Option B: the right trigger is the talk button; E stays on the keyboard.
